name: Secularism
summary: Political secularism holds that religion and government should be kept separate: the state recognises and funds no religion, enforces no religious law, protects freedom of conscience and treats believers and non-believers equally. Its strands range from the separationist US model and the strict French laïcité to accommodationist models in which the state supports religion impartially.
scope: Mainstream political secularism as a church-state doctrine, drawing on George Holyoake's English Secularism (1896), the 1905 French separation law and the liberal-democratic literature. It excludes state atheism, which Wikipedia notes may not count as secularism. Most answers outside religion and state are low-confidence inferences.

refugee-return.rationale: Secularism has no stated position on refugee return; adherents differ.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Secularism favours civic, not ethnic, membership of the state, so nationality-based territorial claims are inferred to be rejected.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Secularism protects freedom of conscience, including leaving a religion; the 1905 French law guarantees it.

women-must-cover.rationale: Neutrality between religions and personal freedom of conscience rule out the state imposing religious dress codes.

common-currency.rationale: Secularism has no stated position on monetary union; adherents differ.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Secularism has no stated position on political unity of kindred peoples; adherents differ.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Strict laïcité opposes separate religious institutions, while accommodationist models allow them, so adherents are split.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Equal citizenship regardless of belief implies minorities claim equal rights where they live; inferred.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Secularism is a view on church and state, not a theory of history; its liberal adherents lean towards ideas and conscience driving change, inferred.

ban-cartels.rationale: Secularism has no stated position on competition policy; adherents differ.

no-bailouts.rationale: Secularism has no stated position on bailouts; adherents differ.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Liberal-democratic secularism protects rights against majorities (freedom of conscience), so courts limiting majorities are inferred to be supported.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Secularism has no stated position on gender quotas; adherents differ.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Secularism has no stated position on economic self-sufficiency; adherents differ.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Secularism has no stated position on trade standards; adherents differ.

moral-incentives.rationale: Secularism has no stated position on work incentives; adherents differ.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Holyoake's secularism was reformist and constitutional, so armed vanguards are inferred to be rejected.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Secularism has no stated position on hereditary titles, though its equal-treatment principle may lean against them; adherents differ.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Secularism is a view about religion and the state and has no stated position here; adherents differ.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Inferred from secularism's liberal-democratic commitment to equal standing and self-government; it does not address colonial rule.

patriotic-education.rationale: French laïcité teaches republican civic values in state schools, but secularism as a doctrine takes no stand on pride in national symbols; adherents differ.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Secularism is a view about religion and the state and has no stated position here; adherents differ.

public-money-creation.rationale: Secularism is a view about religion and the state and has no stated position here; adherents differ.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Secularism is a view about religion and the state and has no stated position here; adherents differ.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Secularism is a view about religion and the state and has no stated position here; adherents differ.

delink-world-market.rationale: Secularism is a view about religion and the state and has no stated position here; adherents differ.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Secularism is a view about religion and the state and has no stated position here; adherents differ.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Inferred from secularism's principle of equal treatment of believers and non-believers; the sources apply it to the state, not private owners, so adherents may differ.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Inferred from secularism's protection of freedom of conscience as a guaranteed right, as in Article 1 of the 1905 law; the entrenchment question itself is not addressed.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Not addressed; secularism is about church and state, with no doctrine on colonial treaties.

elective-rulers.rationale: Inferred from the secular view that political authority comes from the people, not from religious right.

minority-veto.rationale: Secular liberal democracy rests on majority rule with rights protections, not on individual vetoes.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Inferred from the liberal-democratic literature on legitimate authority, which secularism draws on.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Inferred from secular liberal-democratic government in which elected legislatures are supreme and religion confers no authority on rulers.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Inferred from the liberal humanism common among secularists; not part of church-state doctrine.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Inferred; secularism has no animal doctrine and its liberal adherents typically accept regulated use.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Holyoake's secularism stresses improving the material condition of people in this life; inferred duty of the better off.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Holyoake's secularism is about engaging with this world and reform, so withdrawal is contrary to it.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Not addressed; secularism does not take a position on world-economy theory.

native-born-offices.rationale: Secular liberal-democratic neutrality and equal treatment of citizens tell against offices reserved by birth.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Not addressed; secularism has no position on development strategy.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Inferred; secularism has no stance on territory, and its liberal-democratic orientation disfavours revanchism.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Secular equal-treatment principles tell against rule by descent group; inferred.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Inferred from the secular-democratic opposition to fascism; not a church-state position.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Inferred from the liberal-democratic condemnation of totalitarian regimes, including their suppression of religion.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Not addressed by secularism; inferred from the mainstream liberal scholarly view that slavery was the main cause.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Inferred from liberal equal-treatment principles; not a doctrinal point.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Inferred from liberal equal-treatment principles; not a doctrinal point.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Secularism, as a liberal-democratic doctrine, holds that its principles of separation and equal citizenship apply across cultures.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Secular liberal-democratic doctrine favours civilian control and a non-political military.

filial-duty.rationale: Secularism is indifferent to family duty; it concerns church and state, and adherents are split on the question.

office-by-exam.rationale: Secularism says nothing on selecting officials, except that religious tests for office are excluded; adherents are split.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Not a church-state issue; adherents are split between liberal and protectionist views.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Secularist reform, such as the French 1792 law and Holyoake's circle, backed civil marriage and divorce free of church doctrine.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Secularism is silent on representative mechanics; adherents are split.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Not a church-state issue; adherents are split.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Inferred from the liberal-democratic framework in which secularism is usually held, which defends private ownership of land.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Inferred from the liberal-democratic framework in which secularism is usually held, which assumes legislative control of spending.

single-official-language.rationale: Secularist neutrality extends to religious and cultural pluralism, though the French laicist strand favours French as the public language.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the liberal framework that treats foreigners equally; the question is not a church-state matter.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Adherents are split: the liberal-neutrality strand looks at intent, while some anti-discrimination advocates look at effects.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Secularism takes no position on consumption; adherents are split.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Inferred from the liberal-democratic tradition's preference for non-intervention in other states' affairs.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Inferred from the liberal-democratic framework, which holds that states decide their own alliances and systems.

corporate-influence.rationale: Secularism concerns religion and state and takes no stated position on lobbying; adherents differ.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: No stated position; liberal secularists and nationalist secularists (as in France) differ on foreign influence.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Population policy is outside church-state doctrine; inferred as indifferent.

residents-only-property.rationale: No stated position on local property rules; equal-treatment principles and local autonomy pull in different directions.

job-guarantee.rationale: Economic policy is outside secularism; adherents range across the spectrum.

democratic-peace.rationale: No stated position; secularists are generally democratic but the doctrine says nothing on foreign policy.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Holyoake's secularism works through law and reform and a civil state enforcing equal liberty, so a general duty to obey just laws is inferred.

non-intervention.rationale: Foreign policy is outside church-state doctrine; adherents differ.

industrial-unions.rationale: Trade-union structure is outside secularism; no stated position.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Equal treatment of believers and non-believers and of every religion is core to secularism, which rejects treating a religious minority as a collective enemy of the nation.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The 1905 French model keeps civil, state-regulated marriage independent of religion, so secularists favour civil marriage rather than abolishing legal marriage; inferred.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Public reason and neutral government are usually taken to require that citizens can see how the state acts; inferred, with no stated doctrine.

local-production.rationale: Local production is outside secularism; no stated position.

informal-organisation.rationale: Holyoake pursued secular aims through organised societies and public campaigns, which suggests organised rather than informal struggle; inferred.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Secularism has no stated view on the relative priority of national and international law; adherents differ.

religious-nation.rationale: Secularism holds that the state recognises no religion and treats all citizens equally, so it rejects defining the nation by shared religion.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Secularism concerns church and state only and takes no stated position on this; inferred as neutral.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Secularism concerns church and state only and takes no stated position on this; inferred as neutral.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Secularism concerns church and state only and takes no stated position on this; inferred as neutral.

defeat-communism.rationale: Secularism concerns church and state only and takes no stated position on this; inferred as neutral.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Secularism concerns church and state only and takes no stated position on this; inferred as neutral.

religion-illusion.rationale: Holyoake's secularism is explicitly not atheism and makes no claim about religion's decline, so adherents are neutral; inferred.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Secularism concerns church and state only and takes no stated position on this; inferred as neutral.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Secularism concerns church and state only and takes no stated position on this; inferred as neutral.

socialized-care.rationale: Secularism concerns church and state only and takes no stated position on this; inferred as neutral.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Liberal-democratic secularism favours neutrality and freedom of expression, so purging words by policy is unlikely to appeal; inferred.

treaties-binding.rationale: Secularism says nothing on treaties with internal nations; inferred as neutral.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Secularism concerns church and state only and takes no stated position on this; inferred as neutral.

majority-settlement.rationale: Equal treatment of all citizens regardless of belief makes state-steered settlement of one group unlikely to be backed; inferred.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Secularism concerns church and state only and takes no stated position on this; inferred as neutral.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Secularism concerns religion and state and has no stated position on territorial claims; the statement's religious ties would be given no special weight, but adherents differ.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Secularism has no stated position on the Holocaust; denial is inferred to be rejected because it is a falsehood and secularism's rationalist tradition holds to evidence.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Secularism holds that the state enforces no religious law, and criminalising same-sex relations rests mostly on religious morality; liberal-democratic secularists treat conscience and private life as protected.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Secularism protects freedom of conscience and equal treatment of all citizens, and in the liberal-democratic literature it goes with pluralism and open political competition.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Secularism holds that the state enforces no religion and protects freedom of conscience; the 1905 French law ended the offence of blasphemy against a state church and the doctrine rejects penalties for false religion.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Secularism has no stated position on colonial rule; its equality and conscience principles are inferred to oppose exploitative colonialism, though secularists were historically divided.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Secularism treats religious duties as private matters of conscience that the state does not impose; a binding duty on every Muslim is not a view it would endorse, inferred from its separation principle.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Secularism holds that the state enforces no religious law and that legitimacy does not depend on religious law, so removing rulers by force for not applying it is rejected.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Secularism is about religion and state and takes no stand on direct participation; adherents range from representative to participatory democrats.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Secularism is a church-state doctrine with no view on whether oppressions intersect; adherents differ.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Secularism treats all citizens equally regardless of belief and removes religious law from the state, which supports legal recognition, but it has no stated position and adherents differ.

assisted-dying.rationale: Secularists have often backed assisted dying as a freedom of conscience once religious law is not binding on the state, but the doctrine does not require it; inferred.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Secularism is held across the political spectrum and has no stated view on the left-right divide.

alienated-labor.rationale: Secularism has no stated position on labour under capitalism; adherents include Marxists and liberals.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Mainstream secularism protects freedom of religion for all and treats believers equally, so it rejects the claim that a religion cannot fit liberal societies, though some strands in France argue otherwise.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Secularism holds that political authority comes from the people and not from a religion, and that the state recognises no religion's claims; the 1905 French law rests on the sovereignty of the people.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Strict laïcité, the model in the 1905 law and its later applications, bars religious symbols for officials and in state schools, though the American separationist and accommodationist strands allow them, so adherents are split in degree.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Secularism has no position on private employment contracts; adherents are inferred to be split.

social-market-economy.rationale: Secularism has no stated economic programme and adherents run from free-market liberals to socialists.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Secularism takes no position on armed forces; it is held across the spectrum and most adherents accept a state military, inferred.

rich-first.rationale: Secularism has no stated position on development paths; adherents are inferred to be split.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Secularism is a church-state doctrine with no foreign-policy position; adherents differ.

missingStatements.text: State schools should not provide religious instruction.
missingStatements.rationale: Holyoake stressed secular instruction in schools and the 1905 French law banned religious instruction in state primary schools.

notes: Accommodationist secularists (India, pillarized states) would answer school-voucher, religious-symbol and personal-law questions differently from strict laïcité.
